query: For a multi-principal element alloy system known for limited ductility in cast forms, propose a processing route and phase constitution that would simultaneously achieve nanocrystalline grain sizes below 50 nm and a dual-phase solid solution structure, thereby enhancing hardness and yield strength without inducing brittle intermetallic formation. For example, the sigma phase was reported to form when CrMnFeCoNi was aged for 500 days at 700 °C, and BCC formed at 500 °C under similar aging conditions. evidence_spans: Formation of the sigma phase was reported by Otto et al., when CrMnFeCoNi HEA was aged for 500 days at 700 °C, while BBC formed at 500 °C, and only FCC was reported to form at 900 °C when held for the same ageing time [ [43] ]. In the microstructure of as-cast alloys, there exist inhomogeneities caused by the partitioning of high melting point/slow diffusing elements from fast diffusing/low melting point elements [ [43] ]. These inhomogeneities give rise to variations not only in composition but also in the solidus temperature, which represents the temperature at which incipient melting occurs.

One lower temperature phase is the sigma phase that formed below 585 °C and remained stable in temperatures down to 205 °C. The maximum volume phase fraction of the sigma phase of 0.1854 was at 430 °C, and as reported, the sigma phase is usually distributed along the grain boundaries [ [42] ].
